author: blu
body: Generates apply-annotations.ps1, phase two of two. It reads the report phase one wrote and a human then edited, and it is the only half that mutates anything.

author: blu
body: Every block carries its source VERBATIM in the report, and a block whose lines no longer match the file is refused. The refusal is per FILE, not per block: a report written against an older tree is stale everywhere in that file at once, and applying the blocks that still happen to match would cut the right lines out of the wrong places. A stale report must be a refusal rather than a corruption, because the corruption is silent and spread across thousands of chapters.

author: blu
body: Nothing is written without -Apply. Without it the run verifies every block and prints what it would do, which is the mode to trust after editing the report.

author: blu
body: Keep the definition count low; see the note in ExtractAnnotationsScript for what happens to the CHECK deck otherwise.

author: blu
body: The header line is file, line range, target, verdict and signals. The verdict is one or two words, so it is captured whole and split after.

author: blu
body: A record is finalised when the next header arrives or the file ends, so the flush is written once and called from both places.

author: blu
body: Verify first, mutate second, and never interleave the two: a file is either wholly consistent with the report or wholly refused.

author: blu
body: A removed block leaves the blank line above it and the blank line below, so runs of blanks are collapsed to one. Without this every extraction leaves a widening gap behind it.
